question: Who among the following led the Indian delegation to attend the 56th Annual General Meeting of the Board of Governors of Asian Development Bank (ADB) along with Investor/ Bilateral and other associated meetings, in Incheon, the Republic of Korea, from 2 to 5 May 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nirmala Sitharaman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nirmala Sitharaman, the Union Finance Minister of India, led the Indian delegation to the 56th Annual General Meeting of the ADB Board of Governors, held in Incheon, Republic of Korea (2–5 May 2023). (निर्मला सीतारमण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Asian Development Bank (ADB) was established in 1966 and is headquartered in Manila, Philippines.

• Its aim is to promote social and economic development in Asia and the Pacific; India is a founding member.

NOTE

• Nirmala Sitharaman became India's first full-time woman Finance Minister in 2019. She is also the Ex-officio Chairperson-type representative for India at the ADB and World Bank Governor forums.

question: According to Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, it is the fundamental duty of every person to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and ______________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is integrity of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties. One of them is "to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India". (अनुच्छेद 51क — भारत की संप्रभुता, एकता और अखंडता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th (parents to provide education to children aged 6–14).

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Constitution and were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

question: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eutrophication.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eutrophication" is the process by which a water body becomes over-enriched with nutrients (mainly nitrogen and phosphorus), causing excessive algal growth (algal bloom) which depletes the dissolved oxygen and harms aquatic life. (सुपोषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Biomagnification — increase in concentration of a toxic substance (e.g., DDT) as it moves up the food chain.

• Bioaccumulation — gradual build-up of substances in a single organism over time.

• Hypoxia — a condition of low/insufficient oxygen (a consequence of eutrophication).

NOTE

• Eutrophication is largely caused by fertiliser run-off and sewage. The resulting oxygen depletion can create "dead zones" in lakes and coastal waters.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters was associated with the series of nine articles known as 'New Lamp for Old'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurobindo Ghose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aurobindo Ghose (Sri Aurobindo) wrote the series of nine articles titled "New Lamps for Old" (1893–94), published in the Indu Prakash newspaper, criticising the moderate policies of the early Indian National Congress. (अरबिंदो घोष — 'न्यू लैम्प्स फॉर ओल्ड')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Aurobindo was a prominent extremist (Garam Dal) leader who later turned to spirituality and founded the Aurobindo Ashram at Puducherry.

• He was tried in the Alipore Bomb Case (1908).

NOTE

• His major works include "The Life Divine", "Savitri" and "Essays on the Gita". He is remembered as a philosopher, yogi and nationalist.

question: The Buland Darwaza was the structure built by Akbar at which of the following places in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fatehpur Sikri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Buland Darwaza ("Gate of Magnificence") was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri (Uttar Pradesh) around 1575–76 to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. (बुलंद दरवाज़ा — फतेहपुर सीकरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is one of the highest gateways in the world (about 54 metres) and is built of red sandstone with marble inlay.

• Fatehpur Sikri, founded by Akbar, was the Mughal capital for a short period and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Other structures at Fatehpur Sikri: Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas, and the tomb of Salim Chishti.

question: Who introduced 'Objective Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jawaharlal Nehru introduced the "Objectives Resolution" in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946. It laid down the fundamental ideals and philosophy of the Constitution. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू — उद्देश्य प्रस्ताव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947 and later formed the basis of the Preamble of the Constitution.

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly; Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

NOTE

• The Preamble declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic ("Socialist" and "Secular" were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976).

question: Raja and Radha Reddy were awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2000 for giving a new dimension to which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raja and Radha Reddy are legendary exponents of the Kuchipudi classical dance form; they were awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2000 for giving it a new dimension. (कुचिपुड़ी — राजा और राधा रेड्डी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village Kuchipudi; it combines dance, drama and song.

• A signature element is dancing on the rim of a brass plate (tarangam).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: 'The Best Mistakes of My Life' is an autobiography of which Indian Actor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjay Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Best Mistakes of My Life" is the autobiography of the veteran Indian actor Sanjay Khan. (संजय खान की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sanjay Khan is known for films and TV serials such as "The Sword of Tipu Sultan" and "Jai Hanuman".

• He is the brother of actor Feroz Khan.

NOTE

• Notable autobiographies: Dilip Kumar — "The Substance and the Shadow"; Naseeruddin Shah — "And Then One Day"; Rishi Kapoor — "Khullam Khulla".

question: Which of the following options contains groups of cropping seasons in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabi, Kharif and Zaid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has three main cropping seasons: Rabi, Kharif and Zaid. (फ़सल के तीन मौसम — रबी, खरीफ़ और ज़ायद)

◦ Rabi — sown in winter (Oct–Dec), harvested in spring (e.g., wheat, gram, mustard).

◦ Kharif — sown in the monsoon (Jun–Jul), harvested in autumn (e.g., rice, maize, cotton).

◦ Zaid — grown in summer between rabi and kharif (e.g., watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Podu" and "Jhum" are types of shifting cultivation, not cropping seasons.

NOTE

• Major Rabi crops: wheat, barley, peas, gram, mustard. Major Kharif crops: paddy, jowar, bajra, tur, cotton, groundnut.

question: A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is plasmodesmata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plasmodesmata" are microscopic channels/tunnels that pass through the cell walls of adjacent plant cells, connecting their cytoplasm and allowing transport and communication. (प्लास्मोडेस्माटा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ribosome — the site of protein synthesis.

• Protoplasm — the living material (cytoplasm + nucleus) of a cell.

• Peroxisome — an organelle involved in breaking down fatty acids and detoxification.

NOTE

• Plasmodesmata are unique to plant cells and are functionally similar to gap junctions in animal cells.

question: Which state topped the medal tally at the 37th National Games event held in Goa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Maharashtra topped the medal tally at the 37th National Games, held in Goa (2023), with the highest number of medals. (महाराष्ट्र — 37वें राष्ट्रीय खेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 37th National Games were held in Goa from 25 October to 9 November 2023.

• The mascot was "Moga" (the Indian gaur), Goa's state animal.

NOTE

• The 36th National Games (2022) were held in Gujarat, where Services topped the medal tally, followed by Maharashtra and Haryana.

question: Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, who became the first Carnatic musician to win a Grammy, is known for playing which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghatam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram (Vikku Vinayakram) is a legendary player of the "Ghatam" — a clay pot percussion instrument of Carnatic music. He was the first Carnatic musician to win a Grammy Award. (घटम — विक्कू विनायकरम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Ghatam is one of the oldest percussion instruments of South India, made of clay with a narrow mouth.

• Vinayakram was part of the fusion band "Shakti" (with John McLaughlin and Zakir Hussain) and received the Padma Bhushan and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Other South Indian percussion: Mridangam (double-headed drum), Kanjira (small frame drum), Morsing (jaw harp).

question: During the Mauryan society, Megasthenes divided the Indian society into seven distinct groups. In which distinct group were the 'king's counsellors' placed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seventh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Greek ambassador Megasthenes, in his book "Indica", divided Mauryan society into seven classes. The "councillors and assessors" (king's counsellors) formed the seventh class — the smallest in number but the highest in dignity. (मेगस्थनीज़ — सातवाँ वर्ग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus Nikator at the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

• The seven classes he described were: philosophers, farmers, soldiers, herdsmen, artisans, magistrates/overseers, and councillors.

NOTE

• The Mauryan Empire (c. 322–185 BCE) was founded by Chandragupta Maurya with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

question: How many other members are there in the Finance Commission EXCEPT, Chairman?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four (4) other members appointed by the President. (वित्त आयोग — अध्यक्ष के अलावा 4 सदस्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under Article 280; it is constituted every five years (or earlier).

• Its main task is to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States (vertical and horizontal devolution).

NOTE

• The First Finance Commission (1951) was chaired by K. C. Neogy; the 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N. K. Singh. The 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya.

question: Bhangra and Giddha dance forms are associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bhangra" (performed by men) and "Giddha" (performed by women) are the famous folk dances of Punjab, usually performed during the harvest festival of Baisakhi. (भांगड़ा और गिद्दा — पंजाब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bhangra is a lively, energetic dance associated with the dhol drum.

• Giddha is known for its boliyan (rhythmic couplets/songs) and graceful movements.

NOTE

• Folk dances: Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Lavani (Maharashtra), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Bihu (Assam), Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand).

question: Which of the following banking institutions played an instrumental role in financial inclusion through microfinance loans and their expansion in India?
option_4: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) played an instrumental role in financial inclusion by promoting microfinance through the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme and its expansion across rural India. (नाबार्ड — माइक्रोफाइनेंस/वित्तीय समावेशन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• NABARD was established in 1982 on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee; it is the apex bank for agriculture and rural development.

• It launched the pioneering SHG–Bank Linkage Programme in 1992 to bring the rural poor into formal banking.

NOTE

• Financial inclusion means providing affordable banking services to all; other steps include the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (2014) and Payments Banks.

question: Deodhar Trophy is given in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Deodhar Trophy" is a domestic one-day (List A) cricket tournament in India, named after Prof. D. B. Deodhar, the "Grand Old Man of Indian Cricket". (देवधर ट्रॉफी — क्रिकेट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other domestic cricket trophies: Ranji Trophy (first-class), Duleep Trophy (zonal first-class), Vijay Hazare Trophy (one-day), Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20), Irani Trophy.

NOTE

• Trophies of other sports: Hockey — Dhyan Chand Trophy; Football — Durand Cup, Santosh Trophy; Badminton — Thomas Cup, Uber Cup.

question: The elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is halogens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are called the "halogens". They include Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I) and Astatine (At). (हैलोजन — समूह 17)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Halogens are highly reactive non-metals; they have 7 electrons in their outermost shell and gain one electron to form –1 ions (halides).

• The word "halogen" means "salt-former".

NOTE

• Group 1 — Alkali metals; Group 2 — Alkaline earth metals; Group 17 — Halogens; Group 18 — Noble (inert) gases.

question: Who among the following married the Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1611 and received the title 'Nur Jahan'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mehrunnisa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mehrunnisa married Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1611 and was given the title "Nur Jahan" ("Light of the World"). (मेहरुन्निसा — नूरजहाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nur Jahan was highly influential and virtually ran the administration during Jahangir's later reign; coins were struck in her name.

• She belonged to the powerful "Nur Jahan Junta" and was the daughter of Itmad-ud-Daulah (Mirza Ghiyas Beg).

NOTE

• Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu) was the wife of Shah Jahan, in whose memory the Taj Mahal was built. She was Nur Jahan's niece.

question: What solution should be used to test for the presence of starch in food?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iodine solution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Iodine solution" is used to test for starch. When iodine is added to a food containing starch, it turns blue-black, confirming the presence of starch. (आयोडीन विलयन — स्टार्च परीक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The blue-black colour is due to iodine molecules getting trapped inside the coiled (helical) structure of the starch molecule (amylose).

• Starch is a carbohydrate (polysaccharide) and the main storage food in plants.

NOTE

• Food tests: Starch → iodine (blue-black); Protein → Biuret test (violet); Reducing sugar → Benedict's/Fehling's test (brick-red); Fat → grease-spot / Sudan III.

question: Which of the following ministries has launched the National Career Service Portal (www.ncs.gov.in) ?
option_2: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
option_4: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Labour and Employment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Career Service (NCS) Portal (www.ncs.gov.in) was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to provide job-matching, career counselling and employment-related services. (श्रम एवं रोज़गार मंत्रालय — NCS पोर्टल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The NCS portal was launched in 2015; it connects job-seekers, employers, skill providers and career counsellors on a single digital platform.

• It replaced the older employment exchange system with a transparent online mechanism.

NOTE

• Other schemes of the Ministry of Labour and Employment: e-Shram portal (for unorganised workers), EPFO, ESIC, and the four Labour Codes.

question: As per Census 2011, which of the following union territories has the highest percentage of rural population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, among the Union Territories, Puducherry had the highest percentage of rural population (about 31.7%). (पुडुचेरी — सर्वाधिक ग्रामीण जनसंख्या प्रतिशत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Delhi and Chandigarh are highly urbanised UTs (Delhi ~97.5% urban, Chandigarh ~97.25% urban).

• Overall, India's rural population as per Census 2011 was about 68.84%.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future". Himachal Pradesh had the highest rural population percentage among states.

question: On which of the following days is National Integration Day observed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 19 November.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Integration Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas in this sense / Quami Ekta Diwas) is observed on 19 November, the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. (राष्ट्रीय एकता दिवस — 19 नवंबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The day promotes national unity, peace, and communal harmony.

• Note: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) is separately observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

NOTE

• Important national days: 2 October — Gandhi Jayanti; 15 August — Independence Day; 26 January — Republic Day; 19 November — National Integration Day (Indira Gandhi's birthday).

question: Which of the following is not a tributary of Godavari River?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kameng.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kameng" is NOT a tributary of the Godavari — it is a tributary of the Brahmaputra in Arunachal Pradesh. The Godavari's tributaries include Indravati, Pranhita, Manjra, Purna, Wardha and Sabari. (कामेंग — गोदावरी की सहायक नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Godavari is the largest river of Peninsular India (the "Dakshin Ganga"); it rises at Trimbakeshwar (Nashik, Maharashtra) and flows into the Bay of Bengal.

• Its total length is about 1,465 km.

NOTE

• Major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari: Purna, Pranhita, Indravati, Sabari; right-bank: Pravara, Manjra, Manair.

question: Who among the following are the target beneficiaries for the 'Vishwakarma Yojana' launched by Government of India on 17 September 2023?
option_1: Individuals skilled in traditional folk dance
option_4: Individuals skilled in traditional folk songs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Individuals skilled in traditional craftsmanship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "PM Vishwakarma Yojana", launched on 17 September 2023 (Vishwakarma Jayanti / PM's birthday), targets individuals skilled in traditional craftsmanship — artisans and craftspeople (Vishwakarmas) who work with their hands and tools. (पीएम विश्वकर्मा योजना — पारंपरिक कारीगर/शिल्पकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It covers 18 traditional trades such as carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, cobblers, tailors, barbers, masons, etc.

• Benefits include skill training, a toolkit incentive, collateral-free credit (loans) at concessional interest, and digital/market support.

NOTE

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) to strengthen and support artisan communities.
